Agent.description:
An agent: a saved agent definition that runs on its trigger or
when invoked, plus where it syncs from and the state of that sync.

config.description: The agent definition itself, in the same schema as its YAML file: identity, trigger, input contract, and the session block.

display_name.description: The raw ellipsis.name display text from the config file.
display_name.title: Display Name

edited_by.description: The GitHub account that last edited the agent, when the edit came from a known user.

last_session_created_at.description: When that most recent session was created.
last_session_created_at.title: Last Session Created At

last_session_id.description: The most recent session this agent started, or null if it has never run.
last_session_id.title: Last Session Id

last_sync_error.description: The parse or validation error from the most recent sync attempt, or null when it succeeded. A non-null value means the agent is not running the YAML currently on the branch.
last_sync_error.title: Last Sync Error

last_synced_commit_sha.description: The last commit the agent was synced from.
last_synced_commit_sha.title: Last Synced Commit Sha

managed_by.description: Which writer owns this agent. "github" agents are defined by a file in a repository and are changed by editing that file; "api" agents have no file and are changed through this API.

name.description: The agent's account-unique addressable name (a slug of its display name); usable anywhere an agent is referenced, interchangeably with the id.
name.title: Name

pending_pull_request_url.description: The open pull request that adds this agent's file. Non-null means the agent is not live yet: it starts running once the pull request merges and syncs.
pending_pull_request_url.title: Pending Pull Request Url

sha.description: The definition's content identity: the version fingerprint frozen onto each session that runs it.
sha.title: Sha

source_details.description: The repository, path, and branch the agent syncs from. Null only transiently, before the creating pull request's file lands on the branch.

updated_at.description: When the agent was last updated.
updated_at.title: Updated At

Agent.title: Agent

AgentConfig.description:
A saved agent, as written in its YAML file: identity
(`ellipsis`), when it runs (`trigger`), what goes in (`input`), and the
`session:` block every session it starts is frozen from. Field order is
the canonical key order for files and `to_yaml` exports.
AgentConfig.title: AgentConfig

AgentIdentity.description:
The Ellipsis product namespace for a config file: which schema this is
(`version`), the human-facing identity (`name`/`description`), freeform
organizational `metadata`, and whether the agent is `enabled`. The
presence of a top-level `ellipsis:` mapping is what marks a YAML file as
an Ellipsis agent (vs arbitrary YAML that merely lives under a
config directory) — see `yaml_is_ellipsis_config`.

`enabled` is agent behavior, not freeform metadata, so it stays inside
the config `sha` (only `metadata` is sha-excluded). Whether a session
accepts messages is a per-run choice (POST /v1/sessions `interactive`),
not a config one.
AgentIdentity.title: AgentIdentity

ClaudeConfig.description: Native Claude Code options for an explicitly selected harness.

prompt.description: The initial user message, passed verbatim. Omit to start an interactive session idle.
prompt.title: Prompt

ClaudeConfig.title: ClaudeConfig

CodexConfig.description:
Native options supported by the current Codex adapter.

Options and capabilities expand only when their runtime behavior is tested.
Unknown options are rejected instead of silently ignored.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for every turn. Omit to use the model default.

prompt.description: The initial user message, passed verbatim. Omit to start an interactive session idle.
prompt.title: Prompt

CodexConfig.title: CodexConfig

ComputeConfig.description:
Sandbox compute sizing. Every field is optional; None inherits the
platform default (2 vCPU / 4096 MiB / 3600s — see DEFAULT_SANDBOX_* in
models/ellipsis/vms/vm_execution.py). A resolved value outside the platform
bounds fails validation loudly (a sync error on the config) rather than
being clamped silently.

`memory` and `timeout` each accept a shorthand string ("8GB", "30m") or an
explicit units object ({gb: 8}, {minutes: 30}); the `memory_mib` /
`timeout_seconds` properties resolve either form to the canonical integer
the sandbox driver consumes.

`timeout` is the max wall-clock the agent may run before its execution is
stopped, capped at 1h (MAX_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS — equal to the default, so
today the knob only shortens a session; the cap matches the 1-hour validity
of the sandbox's GitHub token). The worker's lease/visibility heartbeat
ceiling is derived from that cap, so a run at the max stays owned by its
worker for its whole life.

Compute currently uses a temporary flat one-cent amount per allocated
execution, subject to the account's existing free-compute exemptions.
ComputeConfig.title: ComputeConfig

ConfigManagedBy.description:
Which writer owns an agent: the repository file it is defined in, or
this API. Every agent has exactly one owner, fixed when it is created and
changed only by linking or unlinking it.
ConfigManagedBy.title: ConfigManagedBy

Duration.description:
A duration as explicit units, summed. Set any of `hours`/`minutes`/
`seconds` (at least one). The alternative to the `30m`-style shorthand
string wherever a duration is accepted.
Duration.title: Duration

EllipsisGrant.description:
One grant entry: a level, optionally narrowed to instances whose
natural key (a file's name, a memory's path, a secret's name, a config's
name, a session's id) matches any of the `match` globs.
EllipsisGrant.title: EllipsisGrant

EllipsisPermissions.description:
`permissions.ellipsis` as a map: resource → level | grant | list of
grants. Levels are hierarchical (read < write < delete), so `write`
includes `read`. An unlisted resource is denied. The whole block is
intersected with the platform's sandbox ceiling at token mint — it can
narrow what a sandbox token may do, never exceed it.
EllipsisPermissions.title: EllipsisPermissions

EnvironmentBaseBuild.description: Create a reusable base, optionally using only selected repository files.

inputs.description: Exact files relative to /sandbox, including the repository name. Only these files are available during build_base and their contents and modes determine reuse. Omit to use all repositories and invalidate on any source change; [] means no repository files.
inputs.title: Inputs

EnvironmentBaseBuild.title: EnvironmentBaseBuild

EnvironmentConfig.description:
Everything about the environment (the sandbox) the agent runs in: which
`repositories` are cloned into it, which environment `variables` it gets,
its `compute` sizing, and lifecycle `hooks`.
What the agent may *do* from that environment is the top-level
`permissions:` block, not this one.

Each `variables` entry names a variable to inject; with an inline `value` it
is hardcoded, without one it is resolved from the account's sandbox-secrets
store. Only the named variables reach this agent; the rest of the account's
stored variables never do. This is how a config brings in the config and
credentials a custom CLI needs.
EnvironmentConfig.title: EnvironmentConfig

EnvironmentHooks.description:
Environment lifecycle scripts, in order: build_base, after_checkout,
before_start. The first two produce reusable snapshots; before_start runs
before an agent starts or resumes its session. Scripts run as the sandbox
user in /sandbox. A nonzero exit fails the session.

Legacy post_start/post_clone scripts remain supported for existing configs;
both run after workspace preparation, before the agent starts or resumes.
They cannot be combined with the new lifecycle fields.

after_checkout.description: Prepare the requested source revision after Ellipsis checks out all repositories, before saving the prepared sandbox. Skipped when that prepared sandbox is reused.
after_checkout.title: After Checkout

before_start.description: Run before the agent starts or resumes a session, after the sandbox is ready. This hook is not cached and adds to session startup time.
before_start.title: Before Start

build_base.description: Build a reusable environment before full checkout. Cached by declared inputs, script, toolchain, resources, and build configuration. A string is shorthand for run with all repositories as inputs.
build_base.title: Build Base

post_clone.description: Legacy session startup script. Use before_start for session setup or after_checkout for cached source preparation.
post_clone.title: Post Clone

post_start.description: Legacy session startup script. Use before_start in new configurations.
post_start.title: Post Start

EnvironmentHooks.title: EnvironmentHooks

EnvironmentScript.description: An inline shell script run as the sandbox user, with /sandbox as cwd.
EnvironmentScript.title: EnvironmentScript

EnvironmentSource.description:
How a session's environment was chosen. None (the field is nullable)
when the config carried an inline environment block and no resolution ran —
an inline environment is not a reference, so there is nothing to record.

Not derivable from the row: `environment_id` says WHICH environment, not
how it was chosen, and is null for the built-in basic sandbox.
EnvironmentSource.title: EnvironmentSource

EnvironmentVariable.description:
One environment variable injected into the agent's sandbox.

`value`, when set, is a literal injected as-is — use it for non-secret
config (LOG_LEVEL, an API base URL). When `value` is omitted the value is
resolved at run time from the account's sandbox-secrets store (dashboard
/ `PUT /v1/secrets`) by `name`, so a secret can be injected without
ever putting it in the config file. Either way the variable only reaches
agents that name it.
EnvironmentVariable.title: EnvironmentVariable

anyOf.description:
One include-minus-exclude set of GitHub accounts: an account matches iff
it is in `include` (`true` = all, a list = exactly those, `false`/`[]` =
none) AND not in `exclude`. A bare bool or list is shorthand for `include`,
so `users: true` and `users: [priya-shah]` both parse.
anyOf.title: GithubAccountFilter

GithubAccountSelector.description:
A selector of GitHub accounts — the `for:` audience gate on react
surfaces and code review pipelines, classified on the stable entity author
(the pusher for `push`, the PR author for a review). `users` selects human
accounts, `bots` selects bot accounts; each is a `GithubAccountFilter`
(include minus exclude, with bare bool/list shorthand).
GithubAccountSelector.title: GithubAccountSelector

GithubAccountSnippet.description:
Sometimes the GitHub API returns a user of github (can include bots)
using this snippet instead of the full GithubAccount model. One example,
is when the API returns a pull request.

This is the least amount of info we need to represent a GitHub account.
GithubAccountSnippet.title: GithubAccountSnippet

GithubPermissions.description:
The agent's GitHub access: the scope of the installation token minted for
its sandbox — the credential `git`, `gh`, and the GitHub MCP server
authenticate with.

By default the token carries the installation's full permissions on all of
the installation's repositories. `permissions` narrows what it may do:
the string `read_only` grants read access to contents, issues, metadata and
pull requests; a map requests explicit levels per GitHub App permission
scope (e.g. `{contents: read, pull_requests: write}`) and may never exceed
what the installation granted. `repositories` scopes the token to exactly
the listed repos, by name (they must belong to the installation).

Restriction is enforced by GitHub, not by Ellipsis: the token itself is
minted with the reduced scope, so nothing running in the sandbox can
exceed it.
GithubPermissions.title: GithubPermissions

GithubSourceDetails.description:
Identifies the file a GitHub-sourced agent is synced from.

Keyed on the repository ID (not owner/name) so repository and org renames
don't orphan the config; resolve display names from gh_repositories at
read time.
GithubSourceDetails.title: GithubSourceDetails

HandlerService.description: The service whose events a handler responds to.
HandlerService.title: HandlerService

InputContract.description:
The typed input contract: what goes INTO a session (the trigger is
when it happens; this is what goes in).

`json_schema` validates customer data sent as `input` to
`POST /v1/agents/{id}/sessions` and stored as `session.input`.
Invocations require input when a schema is declared. React agents
cannot declare schemas: the platform defines their event payloads.

`message` is the initial-message template: exact `{{path}}` substitution
over the caller payload (or, on a react agent, over the surface's
published fields), no conditionals/loops/filters. Refs are validated at
deploy time against the governing field set (see AgentConfig's
`_check_input`).
InputContract.title: InputContract

Level.description:
What may be done to a resource. Strictly ordered: a grant at one level
includes every level below it (write-only would be a phantom capability —
no real client can create what it cannot read back).
Level.title: Level

McpRemoteServer.description:
A bring-your-own remote MCP server: the harness talks HTTP to `url`.
Nothing runs in the sandbox image. `headers` carry static auth (e.g.
`Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}`); values may embed `${NAME}` secret
references, resolved at run time from the account's secrets store.
McpRemoteServer.title: McpRemoteServer

McpServerRef.description:
One built-in MCP server this agent opts into by name (`linear`/`slack`).
A name reference over the connected built-in set — the platform manages the
server's transport and credentials. It only matters when the named
integration is set to `opt_in` inclusion; an integration in the default
`all_sessions` mode is added regardless. For a server the platform does not
provide, define it instead (`McpStdioServer` /
`McpRemoteServer`).
McpServerRef.title: McpServerRef

McpStdioServer.description:
A bring-your-own stdio MCP server: the harness spawns `command` inside
the sandbox and speaks JSON-RPC over its stdin/stdout. The command must be
runnable in the sandbox image — install its runtime via `hooks.build_base` /
`hooks.after_checkout` if the managed environment lacks it.

`env` values may embed `${NAME}` references, resolved at run time from the
account's secrets store (see `mcp_secret_refs`); everything else is passed
literally.
McpStdioServer.title: McpStdioServer

MemorySize.description:
A memory size as explicit units, summed (binary: 1GB = 1024MB = 1024MiB).
Set any of `gb`/`mb` (at least one). The alternative to the `8GB`-style
shorthand string.
MemorySize.title: MemorySize

OutputConfig.description: JSON Schema for the harness's structured result, when certified.
OutputConfig.title: OutputConfig

PermissionsConfig.description:
What the agent is allowed to touch, per credential the platform mints
into its sandbox. Distinct from `environment:`, which is where the agent
runs; this is what it may do from there.

`ellipsis` scopes the sandbox's Ellipsis API token
(`ELLIPSIS_API_TOKEN`, what the in-sandbox `agent` CLI authenticates
with). `true` / the string `all` (the default) grant the full sandbox
ceiling — everything a sandbox token can ever do. A map narrows it per
resource (see `EllipsisPermissions`); the minted token carries
the intersection, so a config can only ever reduce access. `false` fails
validation — an agent with no API token cannot report its own progress.

`github` scopes the sandbox's GitHub installation token (`GH_TOKEN`) —
see `GithubPermissions`. GitHub enforces it at mint time.
PermissionsConfig.title: PermissionsConfig

PromptBlockedReason.description: Why direct prompting is refused. Absent when prompting is allowed.
PromptBlockedReason.title: PromptBlockedReason

anyOf.description:
The watch scope of a trigger, by repository name (owner defaults to the
account). Include minus exclude: `include: []` (the default) covers every
repository of the installation, so `exclude`-only means "all except these"
and keeps covering repositories added to the org later. A bare list is
shorthand for `include`.
anyOf.title: RepositoryFilter

Resource.description:
Everything a credential can be granted access to, one value per /v1
resource family. `TOKENS` is reserved for the future token-management
routes; nothing maps to it yet.
Resource.title: Resource

SandboxCacheTier.description:
Which image-cache tier a sandbox creation took — the customer-facing
names for `create_sandbox_from_default`'s exact / latest / default tiers.
Rides on `Sandbox.cache_tier` and the sandbox_ready lifecycle record.
SandboxCacheTier.title: SandboxCacheTier

Session.description:
An agent session: one conversation with an agent, from trigger to
terminal state. Returned by `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` and carried by the
session stream's `session`/`snapshot` frames — REST and stream never
disagree about what a session looks like.

agent.description: The agent the session was started from, or null for a raw session started with POST /v1/sessions.

attribution.description: The principal this session is attributed to.

budget.description: The spend budget enforced for this session, in US dollars, after resolving defaults and ceilings.
budget.title: Budget

claude_code.description: Claude Code input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code or codex.

codex.description: Codex input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code or codex.

cost.description: What the session cost, in millicents, broken down by leg and carrying its own total.

environment.description: The full environment configuration frozen when the session was created, with the saved environment's id and how it was chosen.

event.description: The typed external event that started the session; null for direct and scheduled starts.
event.title: Event

git.description: What the session did to git, one entry per repository in its workspace: the commit and branch it sits on, per-file line counts for its uncommitted changes, and the pull requests it opened. Null if nothing was ever captured.

handler.description: The saved handler and its effective display name when this session started, frozen at creation. Null for built-in responders, legacy sessions, and sessions started without a handler.

lifecycle.description: The session's activity, conversation state, messaging policy, outcomes, and timestamps.

output.description: The structured-output exit contract for this session.

parent.description: The predecessor session this session continues; null when there is none.

permissions.description: What the session may touch, per minted credential.

source.description: Where the session came from (e.g. react, web, api, cli, mention, cron).

summary.description: The latest live summary of the session's progress while it runs, and when it was generated.

tokens.description: The tokens the session spent and the model they went to. `total` includes the prompt-cache lanes.

Session.title: Session

SessionAgent.description:
The agent this session was started from: the definition frozen
when the session was created, and the saved agent it came from as it
exists NOW. They diverge legitimately — a YAML edit after the session
started leaves the pointer describing something the session never ran.

config.description: The agent definition the session was started from, frozen when the session was created.

id.description: Identifier of the saved agent this session's snapshot was taken from. Null for a routing-file agent, a code-review stage agent, or the built-in mention agent, which have no saved agent behind them. Points at the agent as it exists now, which may have changed since.
id.title: Id

SessionAgent.title: SessionAgent

SessionArchived.description: When the session was archived and the GitHub user who archived it.

by.description: The GitHub user who archived the session; null if unknown or unavailable.

SessionArchived.title: SessionArchived

SessionAttribution.description:
The principal a session is attributed to: what kind, its id, and — when
the kind is a GitHub user — the resolved display snippet.

id.description: Identifier of the principal the session is attributed to.
id.title: Id

type.description: Kind of principal the session is attributed to (e.g. a GitHub user or an API key).

user.description: The GitHub user the session is attributed to, resolved at read time. Null when the attribution is not a GitHub user.

SessionAttribution.title: SessionAttribution

SessionConfig.description:
What one session runs on: its selected harness, where it runs, what it
may touch, its skills, its exit contract, and its spend cap. Every session
freezes one of these (`sessions.session_config`); an agent
carries one under `session:` (`AgentConfig.session`); and
`POST /v1/sessions` is this shape flattened onto the request body, plus the
run settings. Nothing in here is an agent's identity or trigger —
those belong to `AgentConfig`.

Field order is the canonical key order for `session:` blocks and YAML
exports: what runs (`claude_code` or `codex`), where (`environment`), what it may
touch (`permissions`), then the rest.

claude_code.description: Claude Code input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code or codex.

codex.description: Codex input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code or codex.

SessionConfig.title: SessionConfig

SessionCost.description:
What a session (or one turn of it) cost, in millicents.

`llm` is deliberately NOT called `tokens`: it would sit beside the `tokens`
object and read as "the token count's cost" rather than "the cost of the
LLM leg".

total.description: The grand total in millicents: llm + cpu + memory + fee.
total.title: Total

SessionCost.title: SessionCost

SessionEnvironment.description:
The environment configuration frozen at session creation, enriched with
the saved environment's identity and how it was chosen.

id.description: Identifier of the saved environment the session's config resolved. Null for an inline environment block or the built-in basic sandbox.
id.title: Id

source.description: How the environment was chosen (request, agent, platform_default; repo_default and account_default on sessions from before those ladders were removed). An inline request uses request; an inline environment declared in session configuration has no source.

SessionEnvironment.title: SessionEnvironment

SessionEventActor.description: The event's initiator, when known; never inferred from resource ownership.
SessionEventActor.title: SessionEventActor

SessionExecutionResult.description:
Outcome of the last finished execution, retained across subsequent resumes.

An execution spans a start or resume through parking or termination, and may
contain several turns. Admission failures also produce a result, even when
provisioning never starts.

completion_reason.description: Why the last execution ended; completed also includes parking an open conversation.

SessionExecutionResult.title: SessionExecutionResult

SessionExitStatus.description:
Why a terminal agent session ended — a finer-grained reason than `status`.

`status` (SessionStatus) is the lifecycle state: COMPLETED / ERROR /
CANCELLED. `exit_status` explains *why* a run reached that terminal state, so
the UI and metrics can tell a budget cutoff apart from a crashed tool call or
a deliberate cancellation. It is None until the run reaches a terminal state.
SessionExitStatus.title: SessionExitStatus

SessionGit.description:
Every repo the session touched. Small enough to ride on `sessions`
and be returned by every session read.
SessionGit.title: SessionGit

SessionGitCommit.description:
One commit the session created in this repo (everything past the
provisioning checkout's sha), captured from the sandbox rather than the
transcript so it stays correct through amends, rebases, and commits made by
scripts. The repo is the parent object, so it is not repeated here.
SessionGitCommit.title: SessionGitCommit

SessionGitFile.description:
One file's uncommitted change, as `git diff HEAD --numstat` reports it
(with intent-to-add, so a brand-new file still counts).
SessionGitFile.title: SessionGitFile

SessionGitPr.description:
A pull request the session opened in this repo, written the moment the
creating tool call's result lands (see extract_session_prs.PrCreateWatcher).
Live PR state (open/merged/closed) is not stored — it lives on gh_prs,
joined via `gh_pr_id` (GET /frontend/agents/sessions/{id}/git). The repo is
the parent object, so it is not repeated here.
SessionGitPr.title: SessionGitPr

SessionGitRepo.description:
One checkout in the session's sandbox and everything the session did to
it, split by whether it survived the sandbox.
SessionGitRepo.title: SessionGitRepo

SessionHandler.description: The saved handler and its display name when the session started.

agent_name.description: The handler's effective display name when the session started: ellipsis.name, or the service default (Slack, GitHub, Linear, or sentry).
agent_name.title: Agent Name

service.description: The service the handler responds to.

sha.description: Content fingerprint of the validated handler configuration used when the session started. This is not the Git commit SHA.
sha.title: Sha

SessionHandler.title: SessionHandler

SessionLifecycle.description: Current activity, conversation state, messaging policy, and lifecycle history.

archived.description: When and by whom the session was archived; null when unarchived. Archiving does not stop or close a session.

conversation.description: Whether the conversation is open or permanently closed. Open does not imply direct messages are permitted.

detail.description: Explanation of the current status, when applicable.
detail.title: Detail

interactive.description: Whether the session stays open after its first turn.
interactive.title: Interactive

last_execution_result.description: The last finished execution's outcome, retained across resumes; null until an outcome has been recorded.

prompting.description: The session's policy for direct messages. Caller authorization and message validation are checked separately.

status.description: Canonical current activity. working means a turn is in progress; waiting means the worker is warm and awaiting input; idle means parked. A failed, stopped, or cancelled execution may leave an open conversation.

stopped.description: When and by whom a stop was requested; null when no stop is pending for this execution.

SessionLifecycle.title: SessionLifecycle

SessionParent.description: The predecessor session this session continues.

session_id.description: Identifier of the predecessor session this session continues, if any.
session_id.title: Session Id

SessionParent.title: SessionParent

SessionPrompting.description:
The prompt-affordance projection. `enabled` answers "would a send work",
and when it wouldn't, `blocked_reason` + `detail` say why.

`surface_name` is set only for MENTION_SURFACE, naming where to reply.
SessionPrompting.title: SessionPrompting

SessionSource.description:
Where a session came from: the credential that started it (web app,
API key, CLI) or the trigger that fired (react, mention, cron). Never
taken from a request body.
SessionSource.title: SessionSource

SessionStopped.description: When a stop was requested and the GitHub user who requested it.

by.description: The GitHub user who stopped the session, resolved at read time. Null if the user is unknown or unavailable.

SessionStopped.title: SessionStopped

SessionSummary.description:
A live one-line summary of what the session is working on, refreshed
every few steps while it runs.

created_at.description: When this summary line was generated. Null on summaries written before generation time was tracked.
created_at.title: Created At

description.description: One-line description of what the session is working on.
description.title: Description

SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

last_activity_at.description: When the session last showed agent activity.
last_activity_at.title: Last Activity At

last_message_at.description: When the session last received a message.
last_message_at.title: Last Message At

updated_at.description: When the session was last updated.
updated_at.title: Updated At

SessionTokens.description:
The token counts a session (or turn) spent, and the model they went to.

`total` INCLUDES the cache lanes, unlike the old flat `tokens_total` which
counted input+output+thinking only and left callers to add cache reads and
writes back themselves (the deleted `tokensTotalAll` helper). Cache tokens
dominate an agent run's token bill, so a "total" that omits them is the
wrong default and produced two competing totals in the dashboard.

cache_creation.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache.
cache_creation.title: Cache Creation

cache_read.description: Tokens read from the prompt cache.
cache_read.title: Cache Read

model.description: The model the token counts are attributed to.
model.title: Model

total.description: Total tokens consumed, INCLUDING the prompt-cache reads and writes — the same basis the token cost is priced on.
total.title: Total

SessionTokens.title: SessionTokens

SettingsRef.description:
A config-declared Claude Code settings.json, resolved at run start and
passed to `claude --settings <path>`. That is the CLI settings tier — BELOW
Ellipsis's managed-settings.json floor — so it customizes behavior (model
permissions, includeCoAuthoredBy, statusLine, ...) but can never weaken a
security setting. Lets a team point the cloud agent at the same settings file
they already use with Claude Code locally instead of re-encoding it as YAML.
SettingsRef.title: SettingsRef

SkillRef.description:
A repository directory containing SKILL.md and supporting UTF-8 files.
Resolved at run start and installed in the selected harness's skill directory.
Explicit skill references require a model with the skills capability.
SkillRef.title: SkillRef

description: Frames on /v1/sessions/stream, /v1/agents/stream and /v1/vm-executions/{id}/stream. Ignore unknown frame types.
title: CollectionStreamFrame
